subject.title: [Bug]: web_fetch reports exact-size responses as truncated

question: Should readResponseText adopt an explicit exact-limit overread/content-length contract so exact-size streamed responses are treated as complete?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the accepted fix changes bounded stream behavior at the byte cap and prior maintainer guidance rejected the standalone inference without a contract or real failing response.

options.title: Define contract and repair
options.body: Accept an explicit overread/content-length rule, fix the helper and tests, and require real helper or web_fetch proof before merge.

options.title: Require real failing response first
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not accept another implementation until a real user-facing response demonstrates the false warning.

options.title: Close the source-only edge
options.body: Decide this source-level boundary is not actionable without observed product impact, then close the issue and related PRs.

recommendation.title: Define contract and repair
recommendation.body: Accept an explicit overread/content-length rule, fix the helper and tests, and require real helper or web_fetch proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He made the same-cluster contract/proof decision on the earlier PR and is tied to recent helper history.
